It is spelled d-e-f-i-n-i-t-e-l-y.

prompt: Choose the correct word: “___ going to the market after school.”
explanation: They’re is short for “they are”.
“They are going to the market after school” makes sense, so the answer is They’re.
hint: Try saying “they are” in the gap.

prompt: Which word is an adverb in this sentence? “The tortoise walked slowly home.”
explanation: An adverb tells us more about a verb.
Slowly tells us how the tortoise walked.
hint: Which word tells you how the tortoise walked?

prompt: Which sentence uses its or it’s correctly?
explanation: It’s means “it is”: “It is time to go home.”
Its (with no apostrophe) shows that something belongs to it, as in “the bird cleaned its wings”.
hint: Can you replace the word with “it is”?

prompt: Which word means the same as enormous?
explanation: Enormous means very, very big.
Huge also means very big, so the two words are synonyms.

prompt: Which word is the opposite of ancient?
explanation: Ancient means very old.
The opposite of very old is new, and modern means new or of today.
hint: Ancient means very old. What is the opposite of old?

answer: Ade asked, “Can I borrow your pen?”
wrong: Ade asked “can I borrow your pen”.
Ade asked, “can I borrow your pen”.
Ade asked “Can I borrow your pen?.”
explanation: Put a comma after “asked” before the spoken words.
Spoken words start with a capital letter and sit inside speech marks.
Because it is a question, the question mark goes inside the speech marks.
hint: Spoken words need a capital letter, and a question needs a question mark.

prompt: Which word is a noun in this sentence? “Kindness makes the whole class happy.”
explanation: A noun is a naming word.
Kindness names a quality, so it is a noun. Makes is a verb. Whole and happy are adjectives.
hint: A noun names a person, place, thing or idea.

prompt: What is the plural of child?
explanation: Child is an irregular noun, so we do not just add s.
The plural is children.
hint: This is an irregular plural, so adding s will not work.
